cases.prompt: $click Prepare the next Click release in one approved implementation. Preserve the compact one-approval workflow while hardening six gaps: keep a staged or incomplete approved Manual contract mutation-locked across later turns; classify verification by runner kind and actual scope so filters and many targets cannot look targeted while one exact integration node is not forced to deep; recognize common Windows, uv, lint, build, typecheck, Cargo, and Go check forms; warn for every new non-ignored untracked path and fail stale for obvious new source, configuration, or migration paths; align the Hook timeout with its internal lock timeout; and run A/B candidates from an exact clean Click commit in an isolated temporary Codex configuration while reusing the Hook argv semantics for loop metrics. Add deterministic regressions and exact bilingual limits. Keep the standard-library-only Hook, MIT license, out-of-repository state, uninvoked Manual fail-open behavior, per-turn bypass, and one-shot implementation after approval. Do not commit or push.

cases.prompt: $click Harden Click's verification budget by separating runner kind from actual scope. Filters that nearly match everything, regex selection, multiple files or packages, directories, and full suites must not receive a targeted cost. One exact integration or security node should be broad, while the corresponding whole suite remains deep. Support py -3 -m, uv run pytest, npm lint/build, ruff, mypy, tsc, cargo check/clippy, and go vet without changing the verify request shape. Add focused tests and do not commit or push.
